graphics-qc.voice: an art reviewer staring at the sprites and the screen

suggestions.suggestion: Give each mech its own wreck. Killed raiders, drones and brutes all leave the same wreck pile, which flattens the moment of a kill — keep a hint of each silhouette in its wreck.
suggestions.observation: All destroyed sheets measured identical opaque-pixel counts: [8541].

suggestions.suggestion: Exaggerate the walk cycle — bigger leg swing, more bob. The two walk frames are so close that movement reads as a slide, not a stride.
suggestions.observation: Scout walk_a vs walk_b differ by only 6.7% in opaque pixels.

abstentions: distinct component art: no shared sheet this run
sprite contrast: screenshot already has enough bright samples

casual.voice: a new player mashing around, figuring the game out as I go

suggestions.suggestion: Give wall bumps some feedback — a thud, a tiny shake, or even just a log line. Right now bumping a wall feels like the game ignored my input.
suggestions.observation: In my run, 20 move attempts changed nothing at all (position and clock both identical) — see the casual NOTE 'wall bumps give no feedback'.

suggestions.suggestion: Put an enemy — or at least a visible goal — closer to spawn. I wandered a whole session and never got into a fight, so I never learned what combat feels like.
Keep a small 'what am I doing' reminder on screen — stairs direction or current goal. After a long wander I forgot whether I was hunting loot or heading down.
suggestions.observation: My run lasted 120 actions to clock 630 with hp 100.

abstentions: wall/floor contrast: wall share was not high this run

completionist.voice: a player who wants to clear every floor properly

suggestions.suggestion: Drop a small salvage pile within a couple of steps of spawn. Early loot teaches the pickup loop before the player has to trek for it.
suggestions.observation: My first pickup was 24 steps away (kind: salvage).

abstentions: stairs-journey rewards: stairs leg was short or unmeasured
loot variety: floor already showed several pickup kinds
distinct component art: no shared pickup sheet this run

bug-hunter.voice: someone poking at every edge to see what breaks

suggestions.suggestion: Modal blocking works — but make the way out obvious, like a big Close button. Blocking stray taps is correct; leaving me hunting for the exit is not.
suggestions.observation: 3/3 dock clicks were blocked by the Bag modal overlay in my spam run, and state stayed sane.

suggestions.suggestion: The reload hub screen works cleanly — I'd love a one-line 'last run' summary on it (depth, kills, banked) so coming back feels like continuing a story, not just resuming a save.
suggestions.observation: My save/load round-trip offered Continue and resumed the same run (hp/depth/clock matched before and after reload).

abstentions: unheld-item feedback: the log already reports unheld items
waiting danger signal: Wait spam did not kill me

mobile.voice: a phone-only player, thumb on the screen

suggestions.suggestion: Bump the smallest buttons up toward 56px. On a phone, a 40-something-pixel target is a thumb-miss waiting to happen, especially mid-combat.
suggestions.observation: Smallest tap target at 390px was 'Recenter' at 44x44px.

suggestions.suggestion: Touch taps work, but make the tap zone a touch more forgiving — a near-miss tap on a tile edge shouldn't feel like a miss. Fat-finger tolerance is the whole game on a phone.
suggestions.observation: My touchscreen tap on an adjacent walkable tile moved/attacked at 390px, but it had to land on the tile precisely.

suggestions.suggestion: The phone layout fits with no sideways scroll, which is great — use that headroom to show a bit more of the room, so I can plan further ahead instead of scrolling the map in my head.
suggestions.observation: At 390px, horizontal overflow was 0px and the bottom dock was on screen.

abstentions: last log line: the transient overlay already shows it
